concepts.name: Product manager role
concepts.summary: Can describe what a product manager or product owner is responsible for and how the role differs from engineering, design and project management.

concepts.name: Product lifecycle stages
concepts.summary: Can explain the stages of introduction, growth, maturity and decline and how product priorities shift across them.

concepts.name: Product vision statement
concepts.summary: Can explain that a vision describes the long-term change a product aims to create for its users and why it guides decisions.

concepts.name: Product backlog
concepts.summary: Can define the backlog as an ordered list of work items and state who owns and maintains it.

concepts.name: User story format
aliases: As a, I want, so that
concepts.summary: Can explain a user story as a short statement of who needs what and why, written from the user's perspective.

concepts.name: Outputs versus outcomes
concepts.summary: Can distinguish features shipped (outputs) from changes in user behaviour or business results (outcomes).

concepts.name: Product roadmap purpose
concepts.summary: Can explain a roadmap as a communication of direction and planned outcomes over time, and who it is for.

misconceptions.text: The product manager is the boss of the engineering and design team who tells them what to build.
A roadmap is a fixed schedule of features with committed delivery dates.
Shipping more features means the product is succeeding.

concepts.name: Writing acceptance criteria
concepts.summary: Can write testable acceptance criteria for a user story so that the team knows when it is complete.

concepts.name: MoSCoW prioritisation
concepts.summary: Can sort backlog items into Must, Should, Could and Won't have for a defined release scope.

concepts.name: RICE scoring
concepts.summary: Can calculate RICE scores as reach times impact times confidence divided by effort and rank items by them.

concepts.name: Kano model categories
concepts.summary: Can classify features as basic expectations, performance features or delighters and explain how satisfaction responds to each.

concepts.name: Product requirements document
concepts.summary: Can draft a PRD covering problem, goals, target users, scope, requirements and open questions.

concepts.name: Now-Next-Later roadmap
concepts.summary: Can build a roadmap organised by time horizons and themes rather than dated feature lists.

concepts.name: Basic product metrics
concepts.summary: Can define common metrics such as active users, conversion, retention and churn and say what each tells you.

concepts.name: Story splitting
concepts.summary: Can split large stories into small, independent, valuable slices that fit within a sprint.

misconceptions.text: Everything in a MoSCoW list can be labelled Must have, because stakeholders consider it all important.
A RICE score is an objective answer, so the highest score must be built first.
A PRD must be a long, complete document that is finished before development starts.

concepts.name: Product strategy formulation
concepts.summary: Can analyse market, users and company goals to choose a coherent set of bets that connect vision to roadmap.

concepts.name: North Star and input metrics
concepts.summary: Can break a north star metric into driver metrics and analyse which levers the team can influence.

concepts.name: Outcome-based OKRs
concepts.summary: Can write objectives with measurable key results that express outcomes rather than tasks, and cascade them from company goals.

concepts.name: Product-market fit assessment
concepts.summary: Can analyse retention curves, survey signals and growth patterns to judge whether a product has achieved fit.

concepts.name: Discovery and validation experiments
concepts.summary: Can identify risky assumptions and choose prototypes, interviews or tests to validate value, usability and feasibility cheaply.

concepts.name: Stakeholder alignment and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Can analyse competing stakeholder demands and negotiate scope trade-offs using evidence and strategy.

concepts.name: Go-to-market plan
concepts.summary: Can build a launch plan covering target segment, positioning, pricing, channels and success measures.

concepts.name: A/B test interpretation
concepts.summary: Can analyse experiment results including sample size, significance and guardrail metrics before deciding to ship.

misconceptions.text: Key results are a list of deliverables to be completed by the end of the quarter.
Product-market fit is a single moment that, once reached, never needs to be revisited.
An A/B test that shows a lift in the primary metric should always be shipped.

concepts.name: Portfolio and investment allocation
concepts.summary: Can evaluate how to split capacity across core improvements, growth bets and technical health against strategic goals.

concepts.name: Evaluating prioritisation frameworks
concepts.summary: Can judge when RICE, MoSCoW, Kano or cost of delay fits a decision and where each distorts it.

concepts.name: Pricing and packaging decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate pricing models and tiers against value delivered, willingness to pay and segment behaviour.

concepts.name: Launch readiness and rollout strategy
concepts.summary: Can assess launch risk and choose between beta, staged rollout or full launch with go and no-go criteria.

concepts.name: Unit economics and growth loops
concepts.summary: Can analyse customer lifetime value, acquisition cost, payback and loops to find sustainable growth levers.

concepts.name: Segmentation and positioning choices
concepts.summary: Can evaluate which customer segments to prioritise and defend a positioning against competitors.

concepts.name: Roadmap communication and governance
concepts.summary: Can judge how to tailor roadmap commitments and uncertainty for executives, sales and engineering and revise them as evidence changes.

misconceptions.text: Pricing can be set after launch by adding a margin to cost.
A prioritisation framework removes the need for judgement.
A launch is complete when the feature ships, with no further ownership needed.

concepts.name: Designing the product operating model
concepts.summary: Can design team structures, decision rights and planning cadences that let product teams deliver outcomes at scale.

concepts.name: Creating multi-year product strategy
concepts.summary: Can create a differentiated multi-year strategy with explicit bets, moats and kill criteria.

concepts.name: New product and market entry
concepts.summary: Can design a staged approach to establish a new product or enter a market, including investment gates.

concepts.name: Platform and ecosystem strategy
concepts.summary: Can evaluate when to build a platform, the role of partners and network effects, and the trade-offs for internal and external users.

concepts.name: Metric system and incentive design
concepts.summary: Can design a coherent system of metrics, OKRs and incentives that avoids gaming and misaligned optimisation.

concepts.name: Portfolio sunsetting and pivot decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate evidence to pivot, persevere, merge or retire products, handling sunk cost and customer migration.

concepts.name: Coaching product leaders
concepts.summary: Can build product management capability by creating coaching practices, hiring standards and decision-quality reviews.

misconceptions.text: A pivot means the product has failed and the team should have avoided it.
Good strategy is a detailed plan that predicts the market for several years.
Tying incentives directly to a single metric reliably produces the desired behaviour.
